guard: the Pi driver hands a once task over at most once: it claims the task into one batch, stops the handoff timer when Pi starts that batch, seals and reports the task when the batch is held, and never sends a held once batch again; the extension's once exit is the driver's shutdown
why: M1 drops the claim from the batch. The task is then still pending when the batch is held, so the
continuation's claim succeeds and the task is sent a second time.
M2 keeps the handoff timer running after Pi took the batch, so a slow provider answer would seal
M3 drops the release from the hold. A batch Pi never confirmed leaves its task claimed, neither
M4 lets the continuation resend a held batch without the permit: the duplicate run.
M5 drops the exit registration, so a once seat whose report cannot land has no shutdown to run.
M6 drops the shutdown a session start takes once the driver is shutting down, so a once exit that found
the context cleared ends no later session.

mutations.name: M1 the batch carries the task without claiming it
mutations.find: const turns = turnPeek && this.mesh.claimTurns(turnPeek.goalIds) ? turnPeek : undefined;
mutations.expectRed: the automatic continuation does not send the batch again

mutations.name: M2 Pi starting the batch no longer stops the handoff timer
mutations.expectRed: Pi starting the batch stops the handoff timer

mutations.name: M3 a hold no longer releases its batches' once tasks
mutations.find: for (const batch of this.batches) if (!batch.confirmed && batch.turnIds) this.mesh.releaseTurns(batch.turnIds);
mutations.expectRed: the held batch's task is sealed

mutations.name: M4 the continuation resends a held batch without retaking the permit
mutations.expectRed: the automatic continuation does not send the batch again

mutations.name: M5 the extension registers no once exit
mutations.expectRed: calling it shuts the Pi session down

mutations.name: M6 a once exit with the context cleared shuts down no later session
mutations.expectRed: the next session Pi starts is shut down
